study_identification_part.si4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with First-Episode Psychosis Using Normative Models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study explicitly states its objectives: to characterize the temporal evolution of cortical correlates of psychosis over a 10-year period and to map their associations with clinical symptoms and long-term outcomes at an individual level using normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this 10-year longitudinal study, we aimed to characterize the temporal evolution of cortical correlates of psychosis and their associations with symptoms. ... Our main goal in this study was to map the associations between brain cortical abnormalities and clinical symptoms over the longer term. To achieve this, we applied a normative modeling approach to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based estimates of cerebral CT of people with schizophrenia spectrum first-episode psychosis and healthy controls (CTRL) in a long-term longitudinal study of participants with follow-up after approximately 12 months and 10 years.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses an existing normative model trained on a large public dataset and provides the citation (Ref 29). For the local reference cohort (TOP study) used for model adaptation, the study describes recruitment from national records, eligibility criteria (exclusion of mental disorders or family history of psychosis), image quality standards (Freesurfer Euler characteristic > 5), and reports the final sample size (218 controls at baseline).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Using pooled data from a collection of mostly publicly available datasets from 77 sites, and 40 435 participants, 29 the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals ... For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross-sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners ... Healthy CTRL from the same geographic catchment area were invited based on national records. Exclusion criteria for healthy CTRL included a history of drug or alcohol abuse or dependency, psychosis, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder, or having a first-degree relative diagnosed with a psychotic or bipolar disorder. ... An automatic quality check procedure based on the Freesurfer Euler characteristic was run on all data and samples with a value higher than 5 were removed. ... A total of 218 healthy CTRL and 79 patients were included in the longitudinal analysis

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is included as a covariate, and sex and scanner ID are included as batch effects in the Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) model used for normative modeling. This approach specifically addresses site and scanner effects in multi-site data.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: To account for site and scanner effects, we used the Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach for normative modeling, 54,55,59 which efficiently accommodates inter-site variation ... we estimated a normative model for each region of interest ... using HBR with age as a covariate, and sex and scanner id as batch effects, to predict CT.
